column4: The section says the person is witness to himself and cannot claim not to know; this ayah stages humanity testifying against itself to God's lordship, so the later appeal to ignorance is specifically foreclosed.

The section treats ش ه د as testimony joining knowledge and announcement, and contrasts visible human state with inward truth; here hypocrites say they testify that Muhammad is God's messenger, while the ayah calls them liars, exposing a true-sounding formula unsupported by their hearts.

The section says 100:10 gathers what is in people's breasts and 100:11 says the Lord knows them; this ayah says whether people reveal or conceal what is within themselves, God will call them to account.
The section says God's knowledge reaches the person beyond what is visible; this ayah directly says He knows what people conceal within themselves and what they reveal.
The section contrasts human sight with the Lord's inward knowledge and names al-Khabir; this ayah says sight cannot encompass Him, while He encompasses sight, and ends with اللطيف الخبير.
The section connects seeing with knowledge of oneself; this ayah says clear proofs have come and whoever sees does so for his own soul, while blindness harms its possessor.

The section contrasts the person's limited sight with the Lord's knowledge; this ayah names God as knower of the unseen and the witnessed. Ayah 13:10 gives the concrete consequence that secret and open speech are alike to Him.

The section says what is hidden in a person is known by the Lord; this ayah says secret speech and loud speech, and concealment by night or day, are alike before Him. Ayah 13:9 names Him knower of unseen and witnessed things.
The section asks what a person knows and answers with the Lord's encompassing knowledge; this ayah says God knows what is before and behind people, while they do not encompass His knowledge.
The section says the Lord knows people beneath outward appearance; this ayah states that He knows what is said openly and what people conceal.
The section says the Lord is fully aware of people and names the Day they return; this ayah says He knows what state they are in and will inform them of their deeds when they return to Him.
The section says the final disclosure reaches what is hidden in people; this ayah says no hidden matter in heaven or earth is outside the clear record.
The section says the Lord's knowledge is of the people themselves and their inward reality; this ayah says the Lord knows what their breasts conceal and what they declare.

The section asks whether the person knows what follows from his state; this ayah answers the deniers of resurrection by saying not even an atom's weight escapes God in the heavens or earth, and that people will be repaid for their deeds.
The section says the Lord knows what is within people, not merely what they show; this ayah names Him knower of the unseen and says He knows what is in breasts.
The section ends with the Lord fully aware of people and their inward state; this ayah links return to God and being informed of one's deeds with His knowledge of what is in breasts.
The section's resurrection scene asks whether a person knows what will be disclosed; this ayah says people stand exposed on that Day and nothing about them is hidden from God.
The section says the Lord knows what lies in the person's interior; this ayah states that He knows what is in breasts while establishing truth over falsehood.
The section says the Lord's knowledge reaches the inward person; this ayah closes its account of God's turning night into day and day into night by saying He knows what is within breasts.
The section contrasts what people show with what the Lord knows inwardly; this ayah says hypocrites fear a surah will disclose what is in their hearts, making the hidden-to-public movement explicit.

The section gives خ ب ر the secondary sense of testing and describes a person as witness to his own ingratitude; after Solomon sees the throne before him, he calls it a test of whether he will be grateful or ungrateful.

The section explains خبرة as testing and says people may see their state without understanding it; this ayah says a person interprets expanded provision during a test as proof that his Lord honored him. Ayah 89:17 corrects that reading by naming his treatment of the orphan.

The section's testing sense is developed through this opposite case: when provision is restricted in a test, the person concludes that his Lord humiliated him. Ayah 89:17 rejects both conclusions and identifies the moral issue.

The section says a person can witness his state without understanding its meaning; after the judgments in 89:15-16, this ayah answers that the real issue is failure to honor the orphan, exposing what the person's response to provision reveals.
The section gives the dictionary branch الخبرة the sense of testing and learning the inward reality; this ayah says life and death were created to test which people are best in deeds.

The section asks whether a person knows what the Day will disclose; this ayah names the opposing stance, denial of the judgment. Ayat 82:10-12 continue with keepers who record and know people's deeds.
The section's human witness and divine knowledge meet a concrete parallel here: keepers are appointed over people. Ayat 82:11-12 specify that they are recording and know what people do.

The section calls testimony a report and says the person is witness to his state; this ayah describes the appointed keepers as noble recorders. Ayat 82:10 and 82:12 give their placement and what they know.
The section says a person is witness to his own state while the Lord knows the people; this ayah says the keepers know what people do. Ayat 82:10-11 establish these recorders.
